items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary / noise / outsider audio
items._cn_summary: 这张作品并非传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头的实地录音集。25位枪支暴力的幸存者与当地居民参与其中，年龄跨度从17岁到67岁，他们讲述自己作为暴力的施加者、承受者或双重身份的经历。录制地点位于一位94岁祖母家的前廊，恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥当日。专辑没有添加任何音乐，仅保留了环境声音：包括蚊虫、飞机降落路径下的轰鸣、街区的氛围。编辑选择直接呈现录音师本人的简短评述与原始素材，避免传统评论的介入。收益将捐赠给反暴力公益组织。项目具有强烈的社会纪实性质，通过声音艺术的形式记录被遗忘的社区，声音设计与即兴说唱元素为内容增添了层次。

items._cn_summary: 古典出身的小提琴家兼作曲家 sachi 在首张专辑中将学院派器乐功底与第四世界、trip-hop 节奏结构并置，形成管弦乐编制与电子化律动交织的声音景观。整张作品以小提琴为核心旋律声部，辅以交响化的弦乐层次与冷色调的节拍编排，呈现出兼具电影感与地下电子俱乐部气质的氛围。编排上展现出对织体密度的控制力，器乐段落与氛围段落之间有清晰的呼吸感。整体定位介于当代古典写作与实验电子之间，适合对跨界融合感兴趣的听众深入聆听。

items.body: The first Wandelweiser release by composer Paul Beaudoin, bright shining light, is now available as a digital album download at Bandcamp. Consisting of the composer’s complete organ works to 2025, the five tracks on this album are performed by Carson Cooman, organist at Memorial Church, Harvard University. Paul Beaudoin is a composer, educator and interdisciplinary artist, born in Hialeah, Florida. He studied at the New England Conservatory of Music and received a PhD in Music Theory from Brandeis University. His music has been performed by the Lydian String Quartet, the Buffalo Quartet and as part of the Piano Spheres series in Los Angeles. In 2015 Paul was awarded a Fulbright Scholarship that brought him to Estonia where he continues to compose and write.Paul Beaudoin writes about bright shining light: “This is not a typical organ recital album. The music moves between fragile resonance, sustained intensity, harmonic pressure, brightness, stillness, and force.” bright shining light is an hour of inspiring organ music that employs all the power of that instrument to draw the listener into a state of contemplation and reflection. The title track of the album opens with a deep, full chord that builds upwards from the lowest registers of the pipe organ. This is a powerful, weighty sound much like the initial sensation of seeing a bright shining light. The notes are all sustained tones, with no perceptible rhythm or beat. The tones in the chord are changing pitch at what seems a glacial pace, but the sound is never static. The chord crowds itself together, suggesting the image of a great cathedral nave reaching ever upwards. As the piece proceeds, higher tones are heard above the bass register, thinning out the sound. The overall feeling becomes more reserved and somber as the piece winds down to its conclusion. The liner notes state that “bright shining light was composed in memory of Alexei Navalny and all those who fight oppression.” There is a definite sense of quiet strength and unyielding resistance here, aided by the perceptive playing of Carson Cooman. The power and intensity of the pipe organ is fully exploited, even without the presence of keyboard pyrotechnics. bright shining light presents a rewarding sonic experience that is both artistically inspiring and resolutely defiant in its realization.et caecitas eorum lacrimas eis efficiet, the second track, translates as “and their blindness shall make them weep.” The composer writes that the piece “…captures the tension between certainty and doubt, inviting listeners to consider the impact of their convictions.” This track continues to exploit the full resources of the organ, opening with a bold, sustained tone in the middle register that is soon joined by more notes to form a chord of intensity and power. These pitches are sustained and vary only slightly once established. At 1:00, a bass pedal tone is added, providing a solid foundation. The texture of the chords thin and thicken as the piece proceeds, reflecting certainty replaced by doubt. At times, the feeling is majestic but without the need for overwhelming the listener with raw power. A high flute tone quietly hangs in the air at the finish accompanied by a soft bass tone that provides a soft landing for this impressive piece. The longest track of the album, at over 23 minutes, is notes of union and longing. This opens with a very low sustained tone, soon joined by a new notes in the middle register. More notes follow to form a lovely chord whose pitches slowly change to create a series of warm and welcoming colors. The tempo is unhurried and the tones are without beat or pulse. At 2:40 some dissonance creeps in as the texture above thins and the low tone in the bass drops out adding an anxious feel. After a short pause, a new chord is formed in the middle to upper registers. The addition of a strong bass tone adds a warm foundation that suggests union after longing. These feelings of separation and union flow in and out as the dissonance in the chords come and go. The chord textures change with and without the bass, while the higher registers dominate to yield a variety of emotional colors. The coming and going of the strong bass tone always decisively shifts the mood to one of warmth and welcoming. When slightly dissonant, the tones in the higher register effectively suggest alienation and longing. Paul Beaudoin writes that “In this piece, my intention was to convey the emotions of union and longing through a delicate interplay of voice-leading and harmony, creating a space for introspection.” The tempo throughout the piece is always slow and deliberate, producing a sense of dignity and gravitas. A very high sustained tone at 14:45 suggests completion, even as the other notes in the chord are searching for resolution. A sense of the familiar is heard in the transparency and consonance of the upper register chords as the piece glides to a peaceful finish. notes of union and longing is a graceful, contemplative piece that gently invites the listener into quiet reflection.stillness emerging, track 4, is written for organ and fixed electronic media. The liner notes explain that “…the fixed electronic soundfield serves as a sonic canvas, providing a rich and immersive backdrop against which the organist paints with musical phrases.” This opens with a soft, low rumbling followed by higher tones that soon join in. As in the rest of the album, these are dense chords that are comprised of sustained tones that slowly change in pitch. The higher tones are most prominent, but very soft with a hospitable feel. Bass pedal tones continue to rumble below, but are almost inaudible. There is a mystical feeling to all of this. As the piece continues, the dynamics in upper notes seem to be slowly increasing, as if emerging. The electronic sounds and the organ blend seamlessly; it is hard to hear where one leaves off or the other begins. A whoosh of wind and a low, recurring scratching in the bass add to the intrigue. The entire piece is quietly serene and the dynamic contrasts are achieved by smooth variations in the texture. stillness emerging ends as it began – quietly. The final track of the album is grace abounding and this opens with a soft pedal tone in the bass. Airy flute tones are heard above in a simple melody and the feeling is both meditative and comforting. Paul Beaudoin writes that “grace abounding explores the concept of grace not as a static, singular experience but as an ever-present force that reaches beyond us, continually flowing and overflowing.” Accordingly, the pedal tone in the bass weaves in and out of the texture with the melody in the upper registers always in the foreground. A sustained, higher pitch often soars above, brightly underlining the melody. At the finish, a resolving chord is heard in the lower registers. grace abounding artfully portrays a process that is constantly at work in our lives, despite our human failings. bright shining light invokes all the majesty of a large pipe organ but expresses that power in harmonic nuance and textural subtlety, drawing the listener into deep reflection as well as into an emotional reaction. Those who appreciate the grand sounds of the cathedral organ will not be disappointed, but should be prepared to find themselves thinking meditatively about this music as well as experiencing its exhilaration.bright shining light is available for digital download at Bandcamp. The post Paul Beaudoin – bright shining light – Album Review appeared first on Sequenza21.

items._cn_summary: 保罗·博杜安的首张Wandelweiser厂牌专辑收录了其截至2025年完成的全部管风琴作品，由哈佛大学纪念教堂管风琴师卡森·库曼演奏。专辑包含五首曲目，作曲家本人形容音乐在脆弱共鸣、持续张力、和声压力、明亮、静止与力量之间流动。标题曲以最低音域的深沉和弦开场，逐渐向上构建，声音如教堂中殿般向上延伸，整体感受从饱满转向内敛收束，乐曲为纪念纳瓦尔尼及所有反抗压迫者而作。第二首拉丁文标题曲目表现确信与怀疑之间的张力，中音区持续音逐步扩展为强度和弦，低音踏板音在约一分钟时加入奠定基础。整张专辑呈现沉思与冥想性的声音探索，充分利用管风琴的力度与音色资源，在缺乏键盘炫技的情况下展现乐器的全部表现力。

items.body: Nilsa named “Sofala” after the province in central Mozambique where she grew up, and the song reaches back to her childhood there, at her grandmother’s place in the countryside with no television and no telephone, days given over to dancing and singing. It rides on Utsi, a traditional dance from Sofala that lives on the drums. Batuque hand-drummers Abel Isaquiel Maria, Argentino António and Wilson Raposo Vasco carry the rhythm, with Michi Wipf on the kit and Gil Mário Nordez on percussion, while Rolf Mosele‘s guitar and André Buser‘s bass weave through, and Dzua Mosele answers Nilsa’s lead in call and response, the Portuguese slipping into Sena, the language of Beira. Nilsa sings herself back into her home region. She names where she is from, Sofala, straight out of Beira, then carries the song west to Búzi, calling people to come with her and meet her sister Laurinda. From there it turns to Dominga de Nhaminga. People call her trouble because she will not stay quiet, standing up to demand her rights, stamping her feet and speaking with her hands until her voice carries all the way to the town of Tica. Nilsa returns again and again to one line: “você não só fala, você faz“, you don’t just talk, you do. Born in Beira, the port city that is Sofala’s capital, Nilsa was one of eight children who built their own instruments and played together. She took her first singing prize at 14, and at 16 joined Djovana, a hip-hop group set up in Beira by two Swiss musicians, which carried her to Switzerland, Germany and South Africa and earned her the name Queen of Mozambican hip-hop back home. She settled in Switzerland in 2001, studied jazz in Bern, and has spent the years since drawing her Mozambican roots through jazz and pop across four albums, from Mamã to Salada Moçambicana. “Sofala” comes now beside a second single, “Emilia”, both of them turning back toward where she began. Stream and listen to “Sofala” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Nilsa – Sofala appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 莫桑比克歌手Nilsa以故乡索法拉省命名这首歌曲，将葡萄牙语与塞纳语交织于传统Utsi舞蹈节奏之上。Batuque手鼓与爵士鼓组、吉他、贝斯形成层次丰富的对话，call-and-response结构贯穿全曲。歌词从贝拉出发向西延伸，串联起家族地名与人物记忆，并以重复句式传递行动高于言语的信念。Nilsa从莫桑比克嘻哈场景出发，后在瑞士学习爵士，四张专辑以来持续将非洲根源融入爵士与流行框架。这首单曲连同《Emilia》共同构成她对原乡的回望，融合传统鼓乐、即兴元素与现代编曲，展现了非洲海岸城市的文化脉络与个人叙事的交织。

items.body:
Breezy new age house by an Antipodean artist with illustrious credits beside Michal Hutchence, Bono, Jamiroquai since the ‘80s, evened out with Kuniyuki and 451 remixes...

"Originally emerging from Melbourne’s post-punk and new wave underground in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Gus Till has spent more than four decades navigating a remarkably diverse musical path. From early electronic experimentation with Third Eye alongside Ollie Olsen, through a pivotal role in the formative years of the global psy-trance movement and collaborations with artists including Michael Hutchence, System 7, Manu Dibango, Todd Terry and Bim Sherman, Till’s work has consistently resisted easy categorisation, moving fluidly between ambient music, downtempo, house, trance and psychedelic electronica.

First released on Japan’s Dakini Records in 2006, ‘Rainsong’ captures many of these threads in a single expansive composition. Built around a pulsating bassline, layered live percussion and soaring vocal elements, the track sits comfortably between the dancefloor and more immersive listening environments. Unfolding patiently across nearly thirteen minutes, it combines hypnotic rhythmic momentum with a rich sense of atmosphere and musicality.

For the B-side, Kuniyuki Takahashi offers a distinct reinterpretation of the original. His remix gradually unfolds from a patient introduction into a deep and richly textured exploration of the track’s core themes. Subtle spatial processing, nuanced arrangement shifts and his unmistakable sense of atmosphere transform the source material while preserving its emotional core."
items._genre: new age house / ambient / deep house / downtempo
items._cn_summary: Gus Till是来自墨尔本后朋克与新浪潮场景的资深音乐人，自七十年代末起活跃至今，曾参与早期电子实验并涉足迷幻trance领域，与Michael Hutchence、System 7、Manu Dibango等艺术家合作。《Rainsong》原版于2006年在日本Dakini Records发行，是一首近十三分钟的扩展性作品，以脉动低音线、层叠现场打击乐与飘渺人声元素构建氛围，介于舞池功能与沉浸式聆听之间。B面收录Kuniyuki Takahashi的混音版本，从耐心的引入逐步展开，通过精细的空间处理与编排变化重新诠释原作核心主题，保留情感内核的同时注入深邃层次。整体呈现出跨流派融合的成熟质感，从ambient、downtempo到house的流动转换，展现了音乐人四十余年积累的多重脉络。

items.body:
Arca's new studio album "XXXXX" arriving via XL Recordings.

"Five years after the twice GRAMMY-nominated KiCk i and subsequent KICK pentalogy, the Venezuelan-born musician, producer, vocalist, and visual artist returns with her first full-length album since concluding one of the most ambitious chapters in contemporary music.

If the KICK era expanded Arca's universe outward, XXXXX turns inward and fractures it apart. Across 16 tracks, the album excavates vastly different emotional landscapes to deliver a body of work that is darker, more aggressive, more experimental, and unwilling to settle into fixed form. Initially conceived as a mixtape before revealing itself as an album, XXXXX embraces contradiction as a core methodology. In the spirit of her previous mixtapes @@@@@ (2020)—released as a 62-minute single—and &&&&& (2013), XXXXX thrives on raw exploration and instinct. It arrives as a deliberate interruption of expectation.

“It seems playful, also mischievous, to interrupt that autopilot,” says Arca.

The album's striking artwork depicts Arca as a biomechanical entity, accompanied by two owls—symbols of protection and the underworld in Greek mythology. Like the music itself, the imagery inhabits a space between worlds where transformation is both terrifying and liberatory. Suspended between posthuman augmentation and raw emotion, XXXXX exposes the mainframe. It is a record born from uncertainty, contradiction, instinct, and surrender—a becoming-machine that continues Arca's lifelong project of redefining what it means to be human both in, and against, the machine.

For Arca, rebirth has never been a metaphor, but a practice. She continues to exist in multiple states simultaneously, collapsing boundaries between human and machine, high and low culture, and experimental noise and pop music. Following her first-ever painting exhibition at London’s ICA earlier this year, XXXXX arrives as the latest transmission from a continuously evolving creative process. Over the last year, Arca has remained prolific: unveiling the double-sided single "Puta" / "Sola"; remixing tracks for Addison Rae, Robyn, and Hikaru Utada; collaborating with Tokischa on “Chama”; and contributing production to Madonna’s CONFESSIONS II. She walked the runways and made appearances at major international fashion weeks, while also composing the original motion picture soundtrack for Stillz’s film, Barrio Triste.

Now, after years of transformation beneath the surface, her next musical evolution reveals itself."
items._genre: experimental electronic / avant-garde / industrial / glitch / pop deconstruction
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Arca继KiCk i五部曲之后的首张全长专辑，十六首曲目呈现出向内探索的气质。整体方向被描述为更黑暗、更具侵略性、更实验化，拒绝固化于任何单一形态。创作方法上以矛盾为核心，最初构思为混音带，后发展为完整专辑，延续了此前六十二分钟单曲和早期混音带的原始直觉式探索路线。专辑延续了Arca一贯的人机边界消解主题，视觉上以生物机械形象搭配猫头鹰，呈现希腊神话中保护与冥界的双重象征。与多位主流艺人合作、为Madonna新专辑制作、行走国际时装周以及伦敦ICA首次画展的经历，构成了专辑创作语境的一部分。整体而言，这是一张试图打破自动化的预期中断之作，强调不确定性、直觉与投降作为创作驱动力。

items.body:
2nd wave dub techno staple Stephen Hitchell meets new wave producer Federson in a back ’n forth of timeless originals and versions.

San Francisco’s Chris Kelly, aka Federsen’s Alt Dub label hosts this passing of the baton/torch with CV313 and Echospace figure Hitchell a sits 2nd release after the ‘Positive Charge’ EP  christened the vessel in earlier ’24. Federsen fronts the session with a smoky, night-driving dub of CV313’s ‘Skycrossing’ in properly classic Maurizio style, especially that scooping bassline, whilst shutting it down with the more air-stepping levity of his dusted congas and distant dub chords to ‘Skyway’.

CV313’s original ‘Skycrossing’ places his mastery of constantly shifting, ever the same, dynamic within its unfurling envelopes, alongside a remix of ‘Skyway’ that plunges upward, outward into billowing electro-acoustic dub techno dimensions.
items._genre: dub techno / deep techno / ambient dub
items._cn_summary: 这张EP是底特律/芝加哥第二浪潮dub techno代表Stephen Hitchell（以cv313和Echospace名义活跃）与旧金山新晋制作人Federsen的联合作品，由Federsen主理的Alt Dub厂牌发行。Federsen以Maurizio经典风格重塑了cv313的'Skycrossing'，烟熏质感、夜驾氛围的贝斯线贯穿全曲，'Skyway'则呈现更轻盈的舞步气质，加入沙质康加鼓与远处的dub和弦收尾。cv313的原版'Skycrossing'展现了其在不断变化却又始终如一的动态掌控力，'Skyway'的混音则向上向外延展，进入电声融合的dub techno维度。整体是一次新旧交替的dub techno对话，扎根于经典传统之内进行有限度的探索。

items.body:
Lovers of ZudRangMa, Khruangbin, and even the White Lotus 3 soundtrack will be enchanted with Korlakang’s chiming, low-slung meld of ’70s psych pop and Luk Thung from the quieter side of Bangkok...

“Korlakang are four young friends from Thonburi, the quieter, canal-laced western bank of Bangkok, where temple bells and river rhythms shape everyday life. Formed from a bond that stretches back to high school hallways and shared university years, the band came together with a sound rooted in Thai traditional music and the warm haze of psychedelic rock.

Their debut 7-inch, Samong Sai, is that rare thing: a record that seems to arrive already aged, carrying the grain and warmth of a forgotten 70s pressing. It seeps in slowly, sweet and chill, like sound faintly coming through a neighbour's window. The kind of music that makes you stop what you're doing just to hear a little more of.”
items._genre: psych pop / Luk Thung / Thai folk fusion / lo-fi
items._cn_summary: Korlakang是一支来自泰国曼谷吞武里区的四人乐队，由相识于高中与大学时代的朋友组成，乐队将泰国传统音乐根源与70年代迷幻摇滚的温暖质感相融合。首张7英寸唱片《Samong Sai》刻意营造出老式压片的颗粒感与时光沉淀的听感，音乐缓慢渗入，如同邻居窗缝中隐约传来的声响，带着甜与凉的氛围。这张作品扎根于湄南河畔的水道与寺庙钟声所塑造的日常生活节奏之中，将Luk Thung（泰国农村流行音乐）的传统元素与迷幻流行乐的慵懒律动交织。整体听感偏向沉静、低调，注重氛围渲染而非旋律突出，是一张带有地域色彩与怀旧情绪的小品式作品，适合在安静环境下反复聆听以感受其层次。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Gianni Leone has remained active since the era of YS, the album for which he is best remembered, and it was in this spirit that Il Balletto di Bronzo returned to craft a highly distinctive work. Rich in nuance and imagery, it evokes a dark, ominous, and theatrical atmosphere; performing as a trio, the band ingeniously constructs a soundscape that suggests specific moods and settings, scenes suspended in time and space where the very concepts of time and space begin to lose their meaning."Oceani Sconosciuti" carries an air of silent-film horror reminiscent of the band Crucis, while the atonal counterpoint found throughout the album also shares common ground with the music of Van Der Graaf Generator. Gianni handles the vocals, lending Lemures a distinct avant-garde aura."L'Emofago" features a powerful drum foundation reminiscent of Led Zeppelin; the atmosphere created by the keyboards and the lyrics of this concept �lbum, which incorporates symphonic Minimoog flourishes and operatic recitatives within a hard rock (bordering on heavy metal) context, complements Gianni's soaring vocals. It evokes lightning bolts and tremors raining down upon Sodom and Gomorrah, all delivered by the trio in this magnificent progressive work. It suggests that the best of the 70s never truly faded away; rather, updated for the present, that spirit remains more vital than ever, especially since the music avoids sounding merely "vintage."Napoli Sotterranea paints vivid mental images, an entire movie, really. Keyboards take on the role of guitars, while the vocals explore mystical Eastern melodies, accompanied by a drum and bass foundation that occasionally borders on psychedelia before embracing jazz-rock, though of a violent, provocative, and aggressive variety. This is not the comeback of an established band merely recreating the past; rather, it is a group intent on offering something new and making a fresh contribution to the musical landscape.There is melody in L'Ombra Degli Dei... ideas are laid out; it is music that is alive, in the tradition of Italian progressive rock, drawing upon its influences to forge something new. Following a keyboard introduction, an instrumental section transports us into a different world; each step of the staircase leads to a distinct realm. "Labyrinthus" blends Eddie Jobson's U.K.-style keyboards with Gianni Leone's operatic vocals, while a jazz section with a Canterbury-esque spirit permeates the entire piece; the trio delivers an impeccable performance, featuring an improvised section where time constraints seem irrelevant, that evokes a chamber-music atmosphere, ultimately allowing that blend of tragic and futuristic romanticism to return and take hold.The intricate, agile keyboard arrangements of "Certezze Fragili" contrast with the dense, suspended atmosphere of "Deliquio Viola," where this progressive-opera fusion is pushed to its absolute limits, akin to reconstructing a Renaissance past using parts from dismantled cars. They achieve the seemingly impossible; all that remains is to follow the rhythm as the keyboards and drums, pulsing with energy, lead us to "Il Vento Poi." There, echoes of the wind sweep the voices away, distorting them and blurring the lines between reality and time, exposing their relativity, and, by extension, their malleability, as well as the possibility of altering them through perception.
items._genre: rock progressivo italiano / avant-garde prog / jazz-rock fusion
items._cn_summary: Il Balletto di Bronzo 2023年专辑《Lemures》延续了意大利前卫摇滚传统，以三人编制构建出充满暗色调与戏剧张力的声景。键盘手兼主唱 Gianni Leone 兼任人声与Minimoog合成器的主导角色，作品将无调性对位法、交响化键盘华彩、歌剧式宣叙调融入硬摇滚骨架。《Napoli Sotterranea》以键盘替代吉他主导织体，引入神秘东方旋律与迷幻段落，鼓贝斯底色在psychedelia与暴力化的jazz-rock之间游走。《Labyrinthus》融合Eddie Jobson式键盘与坎特伯雷式爵士即兴，在室内乐氛围中展开时间感消融的器乐段落。整体试图在致敬70年代遗产的同时避免纯粹的复古复刻，以歌剧-前卫摇滚融合的方式将文艺复兴意象与未来主义浪漫主义并置。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)
items.label: Analog Africa
items._cn_summary: Analog Africa 第44号发行，收录贝宁创作人 Antoine Dougbé 与 Cotonou 节奏管弦乐队于1977至1982年间合作的录音。Dougbé 以击腿节奏 Cavacha 闻名，其灵感来自鼓手 Belobi Meridjo 从火车节拍中提炼的律动，这一节奏模式在1970年代中期席卷刚果流行乐坛。他自称"恶魔首相"，笃信伏都教，与 Poly-Ritmo 独家合作的原因在于他坚信该乐队是唯一能精准呈现其音乐理念的团队。专辑虽仅有三张正式作品与若干单曲，却浓缩了极强的音乐能量。编曲中可辨识出古巴 son 影响的痕迹，合成器与塑料质感的吉他音色贯穿其中，刚果伦巴的律动在曲目里清晰浮现。Analog Africa 作为专注非洲与拉丁美洲冷门音乐的独立厂牌，在抢救与传播此类文化遗产方面持续投入，此辑延续了厂牌对 Poly-Ritmo 此前三张精选的整理脉络，为 Dougbé 这位短暂却浓烈的音乐生涯提供了国际化的聆听入口。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items._genre: musette / French chanson / jug band / ragtime / eclectic folk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dominique Cravic与未来原始人乐队录制，是一张无法归类的作品，将法国bal-musette传统与拉格泰姆、jug band、法国香颂、skiffle等风格融为一体。乐手在巴黎一间咖啡馆式的想象中诞生了这支乐队，封面由地下漫画家Robert Crumb绘制。27首短曲以人声为核心，伴以手风琴、萨克斯、班卓琴、尤克里里、锯琴、簧风琴等老式乐器，整体呈现出翻找78转唱片柜的怀旧质感。曲目涵盖1920年代老歌翻唱与原创致敬，包括对已故法国抵抗运动传奇女歌手Juliette Gréco的追忆。乐评将其与Dan Hicks & His Hot Licks相提并论，强调表演者以严肃态度对待这些被遗忘的音乐类型。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合的数字EP处女作，由北欧民谣圈资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统音乐素材，乐手各自带入不同的诠释视角，营造出古老而略带粗粝的听觉氛围。开场曲以粗犷的奔跑节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；唯一的原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，加入口弦与风笛形成持续推进的动力。匈牙利扬琴为传统曲目提供精致的音色背景，口弦的柔软质感在器乐曲中与笛和弦乐交织，产生略带失衡的趣味张力。整体而言，这个仅五曲的短篇呈现了一个早熟而沉稳的乐队雏形，暗示了后续全长专辑的潜力。

Buraka Som Sistema have spent most of that decade apart, and on Friday 7 August they walk back onto a UK stage at South London Miniteca: a free, all-day celebration of the Latin American and Afro-Luso communities of South London, out in the open in Burgess Park. items.body: Ten years is a long time to leave a dancefloor waiting. Buraka Som Sistema have spent most of that decade apart, and on Friday 7 August they walk back onto a UK stage at South London Miniteca: a free, all-day celebration of the Latin American and Afro-Luso communities of South London, out in the open in Burgess Park. Pulling the Main Stage together from midday are ¡Como No!, the capital’s leading Latin promoter since the 1980s and the outfit behind La Linea. The Lisbon crew spent the late 2000s welding Angolan kuduro to European club music, a sound that reached far past Portugal on tracks like “Sound of Kuduro“, made with M.I.A., “Hangover (BaBaBa)“, and “Kalemba (Wegue Wegue)“. Their 2008 album Black Diamond set the template, and two more followed, Komba in 2011 and Buraka in 2014. Years of touring took them from Caracas to Paris, India and Luanda, filmed across those cities in Off the Beaten Track, with an MTV Europe Music Award picked up along the way. They stepped away in 2016 and scattered into solo work, with Branko steering the Enchufada label and Kalaf turning to writing and cultural work. This summer they regrouped for the label’s twentieth anniversary and released “Puro Mambo”, an Angolan-slang title and their first new music in twelve years, alongside a run of festival dates and the first vinyl pressing of their full catalogue. Blaya, whose voice became part of the group’s identity as it grew, is back out front. Where Buraka bent kuduro, Son Rompe Pera bend cumbia, running their marimbas through punk. The second headliners of the festival, the Gama brothers grew up playing the wooden keys at weddings and quinceañeras in Naucalpan, on the edge of Mexico City, alongside their father Batuco; as teenagers they swapped it for punk, then dragged the marimba back with all that noise attached. After Batuco’s death, an invitation from Chilean cumbia veterans Chico Trujillo in 2017 pulled them back to music, and the cumbia punk they play now tips traditional Mexican and pan-Latin songs into garage, ska and surf. A new album, Marimbazos de Oro, follows in September on Mixto Records, produced by the Black Pumas’ Adrian Quesada, with lead single “Nada Que Hacer”. Live, they pull cumbia dancers and moshers to the same marimba. If Lisbon and Mexico City set the day’s coordinates, the rest of the Main Stage answers from London itself. Pianist Eliane Correa built Las Salseras here as the UK’s first all-female salsa orchestra, ten players drawn from across Latin America and the UK. Cuban percussionists Madelin Espinosa and Lidia María Madruga anchor the rhythm section with Argentine multi-percussionist Gala Celia, and Afro-Latin singer Juanita Euka takes the front, a voice that has carried this music at the Barbican and Glastonbury. Between them they have backed Los Van Van’s Mayito Rivera and Jimmy Bosch and tour with Hans Zimmer and Jessie Ware. Correa, who counts herself as much Argentinian and European as Cuban, is blunt about the all-women line-up, “We are not tokens”, a counterweight to the male bands salsa has run on for most of its life. They mark Celia Cruz’s centenary with “La Vida es un Carnaval” and “Quimbara”, alongside Tito Puente’s “Oye Cómo Va” and deeper cuts from the Queen of Salsa’s catalogue. Latinas of London brings a second all-women line-up to the stage, with Allexa Nava crossing over from the salsa orchestra. Desta French runs it on one rule, Latinas backing Latinas, no one above anyone else. A Camden singer of Colombian and Italian parentage, she was the first UK Latin artist played on BBC Radio with an all-Spanish-language song, back in 2020; she writes across jazz, hip-hop and cumbia, and her nights at the Jazz Café have turned into full-room Selena singalongs. Alongside Nava she brings Xativa, whose folk-leaning songs draw on Spanish and Ecuadorian roots. A second stage, Bailoteo, is given over to Latin American sound system culture, run by Bushbby, who started the Candelita night with Desta French. London-born with Colombian roots, she plays cumbia, champeta, reggaetón and dembow off the systems she grew up around. DJ Sueño joins her with the cumbiatón he sharpened in Rosa Pistola’s Mexico City circle, Sabor a Mi runs from guaguancó through cumbia to afro-house on vinyl, and Movimientos resident Amancai, who grew up in Cartagena, threads Colombian Caribbean sounds through afrobeats. Between sets there are children’s sports, yoga and stretching sessions, DJ workshops and food from across the Latin and Lusophone world, open to every age.   South London Miniteca runs from 12pm at Burgess Park on 07/08 Entry is free, though tickets should be booked ahead. Full details and booking are on Dice   https://rhythmpassport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AQN_OqLUuwDQPUykEz7IUF2r_or88TQL8tbWQhzbPiELPxiEZiU8w35P2el5YbcOlFqi1_i3NMCPm9nlnYpo5A10H8oyG-kr4Jq8Pl4.mp4 The post Event Preview: South London Miniteca @ Burgess Park (London; Friday, 7th August 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Review by alainPP — SYRINX CALL operates outside of time, with flutes galore exuding a strong folk vibe; Mirrorneuron is an empathy-dispensing AI controlled by Mara?an intricate psychotherapist figure in this supernatural fable that echoes the style of SINGLE CELLED ORGANISM.'Returning' kicks off with a SINGLE CELLED ORGANISM feel?fitting, given the flute that defines the band's signature atmosphere. It's modern progressive rock?layered and ethereal?flowing into'Boundless Choices,' where Kate Bush and Pink Floyd hover in the background alongside warm vocals; a blend of prog and neo-classical styles featuring swirling guitars and an enchanting flute.'Organic Embodiment' carries hints of ANGE in its melody, while Hannes's heavy build-up evokes ELOY. Jens's velvety vocals briefly recall the soaring heights of SYLVAN or classic-era MARILLION. The whole track is sprinkled with flute and female vocalizations.'Are You My Image' features female vocals and an ambient folk-pop sound reminiscent of ENYA or IONA?truly magical; the guitar arpeggios and flute create a moment of simple, ineffable beauty.'Wheels of Emotion' follows, with narration set against the flute, leading to an emotional breakdown featuring a guitar solo that appears out of nowhere?a solemn moment touching greatness, with sharp guitar work reminiscent of MARILLION. The flute-driven folk drift shares this medieval-troubadour-style track with a big 80s-style keyboard solo and a dash of *Different Light*-era vibes.'Yearning' continues the conceptual journey, with the AI ​​narrating the atmospheric space setting. It is a long, building track?saccharine-sweet in its vocals, yet solid and substantial in its instrumentation. The finale, featuring Isgaard's spellbinding vocals, is truly outstanding. "Attachment," featuring Doris, offers a pastoral ballad reminiscent of days gone by?think JADIS or ELOY?showcasing languid six-string work that flirts with a Floydian atmosphere. The keyboards strongly evoke ELOY?delivering that weighty sound perfect for navigating the landscape of German progressive rock?followed by another Floydian outro featuring waves of sound."Emptiness" follows, led by the alto flute for a gentle, melancholic interlude; Isgaard once again takes center stage with an elven vocal performance over a crystalline piano finale."Mind Over Matter" comes next, blending flute and piano into another melting folk-prog excursion, with Jens's keyboard touches guiding the listener toward a heroic fantasy realm; it is an ethereal ballad that eventually crashes into..."Here..." an interlude defined by its dark alto flute?a moment of suspended anticipation."...And Now" brings back the energy with a soft-heavy riff and reverb-laden guitar, recalling the New Age sounds of APSARAS. The melody begins to circle back on itself slightly, though one must acknowledge that sustaining an hour of such high quality is no small feat. It is time to leave; cinematic footsteps sound before Isgaard calls us to..."The Difference," a track redolent of Kate Bush; the epilogue to a musical odyssey, complete with laughter, tears, doubt, and hope.SYRINX CALL has released a musical gem that builds upon the foundation of their previous album. It is a slow musical journey where the tracks weave a spell, causing you to lose yourself and fall under their hypnotic influence. The sound is an energetic and glamorous blend of folk, rock, and prog?sharp, effective, and polished. (4.75)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以横笛为核心音色，构建了一个围绕AI心理治疗师展开的概念叙事。音乐将民谣旋律、新世纪氛围与古典元素编织在一起，呈现出长篇架构化的前卫摇滚体验。编曲层次丰富，键盘铺底厚重，吉他与笛声交织出中世纪游吟诗人式的质感。多首曲目邀请女性人声献唱，形成与主唱声线的对比融合。整体风格偏向德式交响前卫的厚重感，同时融入英国前卫的诗意与旋律性。作为跨界前卫作品，其制作精良，概念完整，但在声音实验性与突破性方面较为保守，偏向类型内部的精致整合而非前沿探索，与极端前卫、电子实验或世界音乐融合的偏好存在一定距离。

items.body:
First re-pressing in years of Mark Ernestus & Moritz Von Oswald’s divine, final Rhythm & Sound release, heeling to tradition with a one-riddim album focussed on its carousel of roots reggae legends; Sugar Minott, Paul St. Hilaire, Willi Williams, Jah Cotton, Bobbo Shanti, and more

In 2005 Rhythm & Sound capped their holy mountain catalogue with ‘See Mi Yah’, a 7 x 7” set and LP which completed a 10 year run of inspired dub productions with their purest offering to the form. At the time, younger ears to their music would be left perplexed by the lack of instrumental variation - but any others with a little knowledge of one-riddim set traditions knew it was their ultimate ode to roots reggae fundamentals, after respectfully messing with the style & pattern across the Burial Mix 10”s (as collected in ‘w/ The Artists’), and the more radical 12” mutations of the Rhythm & Sound series, proper, since 1996 (not to mention birthing dub house-techno before that).     

Seeing off the project in fine style, Ernestus & Von Oswald gave studio time to their favourite vocalists, generating a slew of original performances displaying the range and depth of roots reggae’s elders and contemporary torch carriers on their signature backdrop of air-trodding bass and powdered dub chords. We were blessed to distribute it in the UK at the time, so many of these cuts are hard etched to the memory, from the ghostly croon of Willi Williams’ title piece thru the gruff gravitas of Bobbo Shanti, the duet between Ras Donovan & Ras Perez, and of course Sugar Minott’s mellifluous reggae soul.

In the year following ‘See Mi Yah’, Rhythm & Sound were naturally elected to edit and master a re-up of The Congos & Friends’ one-riddim album ’Fisherman Style’ for our then warehouse neighbours Blood & Fire Records, sealing their era of roots reflection by appropriately saluting the originators, in parallel to their Wackies reissue scheme, and before Ernestus (and Mark Ainley) would go on to found the more digi-devoted reissue label, Dug Out. Some 20 years of satisfaction later, time has proven this album holds its meditative weight.
items._genre: dub / roots reggae / electronic dub / minimal techno
items._cn_summary: 这是Rhythm & Sound（Mark Ernestus与Moritz Von Oswald）2005年发行的最终专辑的再版。整张专辑围绕同一个riddim节奏展开，回归dub与根源雷鬼的本质。两位制作人邀请了Sugar Minott、Paul St. Hilaire、Willi Williams、Jah Cotton、Bobbo Shanti等多位根源雷鬼歌手，在标志性的低沉贝斯与稀疏和弦伴奏下录唱。评论追溯了两人自1996年以来从dub house-techno到更激进的12寸变体的演化路径，指出此作是对根源雷鬼传统的致敬，而非风格创新。专辑在发行次年又参与编辑了Congos的《Fisherman Style》再版，完成了对根源的回溯。文笔扎实，信息量充足，但音乐本身偏向传统回归，缺乏新的声音探索。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The man who would fall to Earth in 1976 never truly stayed in one place; London, Detroit, Los Angeles, and Berlin always hosted him merely as a temporary traveler, a restless tenant destined to leave sooner or later. It was in this context that, after bidding farewell to Ziggy Stardust, he moved forward with that same band, featuring Mick Ronson, Trevor Bolder, and Mick Woodmansey, but also Ken Fordham on sax, three backing vocalists, and Mike Garson on piano, whose contribution would make all the difference.Naturally, lessons with Lindsay Kemp, the British dancer, actor, mime, choreographer, and set designer, helped shape the persona of Aladdin Sane, a character that offered a critique of the entertainment world and was inspired by the very tour during which the songs comprising the album were written.That same dichotomy, between the lightning bolt across his face and his stance regarding his newfound stardom, ultimately extended to the music itself; one can distinguish between Rolling Stones-esque blues-soul rockers like "Watch That Man," "Panic in Detroit," "Cracked Actor," a fast-paced glam version of "Let's Spend the Night Together," and "The Jean Genie," and other, more experimental tracks. The latter reveal the jazz-inflected and at times atonal influence of Mike Garson, as well as a cabaret DNA and darker, more evocative, compositionally complex themes, songs like "Aladdin Sane (1913-1938-197?)," "Time" (heavily influenced by Jacques Brel, an essential reference for understanding one of his earthly personas), "The Prettiest" (evoking the 1950s, a style that kept coming and going), and "Lady Grinning," a gem featuring a flamenco-style introduction. Both Mick Ronson on guitar and Mike Garson on piano earned their pivotal roles in creating that special magic, an artistic expression that would eventually lead him to portray Paul Ambrosius von Przygodski in the 1978 film Just a Gigolo: a young Prussian character drifting between two worlds yet finding a true home in neither, never fully belonging, much like Aladdin Sane.
items._genre: glam rock / art rock / jazz-inflected rock / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了Ziggy Stardust时期的核心阵容，但将音乐推向了更具张力的方向。专辑可清晰划分为两类：模仿Rolling Stones式蓝调灵魂摇滚的曲目如Watch That Man、Panic in Detroit，以及更具实验性的作品。后者体现了Mike Garson爵士影响下的无调性钢琴语言，融入cabaret美学与更为阴暗复杂的作曲结构。Aladdin Sane同名曲展示了爵士化的器乐推进，Time深受Jacques Brel影响，Lady Grinning则以弗拉门戈式开场。Mick Ronson的吉他与Garson的钢琴共同构筑了这种独特的艺术张力，既是对娱乐工业的批判，也是对明星身份悖论的探索。作为跨界融合作品，它在摇滚框架内引入了爵士与剧场元素，但整体仍植根于主流摇滚语境。

items.body: Review by AWizardATrueAimee — I've got quite the history with this album since my husband, who introduced me to progressive rock, had an email referring to it. That was back in 2009 and I've listened to it countless times since. I was so excited to see the band was releasing a remaster and I certainly have not been disappointed by it. Steve Wilson did such a great job on their other releases. I'll admit I was heartbroken but understanding that this album could present some difficulties. There's been some concerns about AI being used in this remaster that I somewhat understand but?. I don't think we'll be getting as clear and true of a version of this album otherwise. And if this is the way it's got to be done, I'm here for the ride. This remaster/remix showed me all sorts of instruments and sections that I didn't hear in the past which I'm really grateful for. An album which at times was previously impossible to parse is now much punchy and emotionally charged than ever. And the album title track has always rang to me as a Gentle Giant staple within their catalogue. It doesn't get much more progressive than this.
items._genre: eclectic progressive rock / art rock / Canterbury scene
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑属于英国前卫摇滚范畴，在编曲上展现出复杂的器乐层次与多段落结构，融合了古典室内乐元素与摇滚乐队的爆发力。评论者着重提及了重制版（由Steven Wilson操刀）如何让原本模糊的乐器细节变得清晰可辨，揭示出此前难以察觉的声部交织与节奏转换。标题曲被认为是该乐队作品中最具代表性的曲目之一，体现了乐队在中世纪音乐素材、对位法写作与摇滚节奏之间寻找平衡的尝试。评论侧重于重制技术带来的听感改善，而非对专辑本身的深度音乐分析，信息量有限。作为前卫摇滚经典，重制版的发布让老听众得以重新审视这张曾被认为难以解析的作品。

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.
items._cn_summary: 本文以Miles Davis与John Coltrane的百年诞辰为契机，系统梳理了两人合作时期（1955-1967）所用贝斯手的更替线索。文章从1958-1960年的稳定合作期切入，以《Kind of Blue》与《Giant Steps》为坐标，重点追溯Paul Chambers的职业生涯——从底特律Cass Technical High School起步，到纽约参与百余场录音，成为Davis与Coltrane共同的节奏支柱。文章详述了Chambers在1959-1962年间参与《Sketches of Spain》《Someday My Prince Will Come》等经典录音的历程，以及他独立于Davis之外与Jackie McLean、Wynton Kelly等硬波普乐手的合作。Chambers最终因药物引发的结核病于33岁早逝。文中还提及他离开Davis后由另一位Cass Technical校友接替的线索。整体属于学术性爵士史料梳理，文字扎实但偏重传记叙述。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由非营利组织Los Cenzontles制作，探索墨西哥与夏威夷之间的历史文化联系——19世纪墨西哥牛仔从加州前往夏威夷群岛放牧长角牛，并带去了吉他。专辑收录16首曲目，包含夏威夷传统歌曲配西班牙语新词、墨西哥老歌配夏威夷语新词，以及原创作品和美国传统民谣。编曲以尤克里里、吉他、墨西哥竖琴和手风琴为核心，营造出统一的声场。Taj Mahal和David Hidalgo作为核心人物贡献了人声与器乐演奏，并与夏威夷本地音乐人Gary Haleamau、Sheldeen Haleamau、Sonny Lim合作。录音在加州圣巴勃罗的总部进行，五天内大部分一气呵成，保留了现场即兴的真实感。Woody Guthrie的《Deportee》被重新诠释为对移民劳工议题的社会评论，赋予传统曲目当代意义。整体呈现了语言、文化、年龄与性别多元的合作精神。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: Kill Instinct will release their second album, “Kill Two: Behavioral Sink”, on August 7, 2026 through Freak Power. The Toronto electro-industrial duo of Phil Gonzo and Lea Ashley had originally scheduled the digital album for September 18, 2026; the release now arrives six weeks earlier. A Bandcamp listening party precedes it on August 6 at 1:00 AM CEST, where fans can hear the album in full, chat live with the band and ask questions about the record. ‘Kill Two: Behavioral Sink’ tracklist and pre-order The 12-track album carries the tracklist “Unauthorized Disclosure”, “Truth For Silence”, “Fragment Of Reality”, “Ignore The Static”, “Master Or Slave”, “Control”, “People You Love”, “Bury It Deep”, “Found Footage” (featuring Alex Sales), “The Optimist”, “Rat Utopia” and “KI-130”. Several of these tracks already reached listeners as singles ahead of the album, among them “Ignore The Static”, “People You Love”, “Rat Utopia” and “Control”, the latter also released as an Apoptygma Berzerk remix. The digital album is available for pre-order on Bandcamp now. Pre-order buyers receive the already-released singles immediately, with the remaining tracks unlocking on August 7. kill.two//Behavioral Sink by Kill Instinct Across the album, Kill Instinct build on the “behavioral sink” concept and the “Universe 25” experiments first cited when the record was announced in April 2026, tracking themes of surveillance, manipulation and fractured identity against the effects of technology on daily life. About Kill Instinct Kill Instinct is a Toronto electro-industrial duo of Phil Gonzo and Lea Ashley. The project’s debut full-length, the eight-track digital album “Kill.One”, was released on February 27, 2025, with a tracklist including “Funerals”, “Parasocial”, “Grip (Tighter)”, “BIG”, “King of Kings”, “Lovers”, “False Deities” and “Paradise”. A steady run of remixes and standalone tracks followed: “Parasocial (Svjet Zéro Remix)” in May 2025, “Paradise (Vakhtang Remix)” in July 2025, “Funerals (Svjet Zéro Remix)” and “Grip (Tighter) [Forged Reigns Remix]” in August 2025, the standalone single “BIG (VIP)” on November 7, 2025, “BIG (Jalex Remix)” and “Funeral Stripper” in October 2025, “Parasocial (Trakt Null Remix)” in December 2025, and “Funeral Stripper (Night Version)” in January 2026. Outside Kill Instinct, Phil Gonzo has contributed remix work to Matte Blvck’s “Vows”. Kill Instinct began the rollout for “Kill Two: Behavioral Sink” in April 2026 with lead single “Ignore the Static”, followed by “People You Love”, “Control” – which also received the Apoptygma Berzerk remix – “Bury It Deep” and “Rat Utopia”. The album was originally set for September 18, 2026; Kill Instinct have now moved it up to August 7, preceded by an August 6 Bandcamp listening party.

items.body: Talking Heads released their third studio album, “Fear of Music,” on 3 August 1979 through Sire Records. The album turns 47 this year. Produced by Brian Eno and the band, “Fear of Music” followed “More Songs About Buildings and Food” (1978) and preceded “Remain in Light” (1980), the middle record of three consecutive Eno collaborations that reshaped the band’s sound. Talking Heads recorded the album’s basic tracks on 22 April and 6 May 1979 at drummer Chris Frantz and bassist Tina Weymouth’s loft in Long Island City, Queens, using the Record Plant’s mobile studio, then completed the record at the Hit Factory, Atlantic Studios, RPM Studios and Record Plant in New York City. Greg Calbi mastered the album at Sterling Sound. The eleven-track album is sequenced across two sides: “I Zimbra,” “Mind,” “Paper,” “Cities,” “Life During Wartime” and “Memories Can’t Wait” open the record, followed by “Air,” “Heaven,” “Animals,” “Electric Guitar” and “Drugs.” King Crimson guitarist Robert Fripp guests on opener “I Zimbra,” whose lyrics set a Hugo Ball Dada poem to music. “Fear of Music” streams on Spotify. About Talking Heads Talking Heads formed in New York City in 1975. David Byrne and Chris Frantz had played together as the Artistics at the Rhode Island School of Design from 1973, joined by fellow student Tina Weymouth on bass after the trio moved to New York City in 1975. The band played its first show as Talking Heads on 5 June 1975, opening for the Ramones at CBGB. They signed to Sire Records in November 1976 and released their first single, “Love → Building on Fire,” in February 1977. Jerry Harrison, formerly of the Modern Lovers, joined on keyboards and guitar in March 1977, completing the lineup. The debut album “Talking Heads: 77” followed in 1977 and produced the single “Psycho Killer.” “More Songs About Buildings and Food” (1978) marked the band’s first collaboration with Brian Eno and included a cover of Al Green’s “Take Me to the River,” which became the group’s first Billboard Top 30 hit. “Fear of Music” (1979) continued the Eno partnership, mixing post-punk with funk and disco rhythms, and “Remain in Light” (1980) closed the trilogy with West African polyrhythms drawn from Fela Kuti’s music, which Eno had introduced to the band. Talking Heads reached its commercial peak in 1983 with “Speaking in Tongues” and the US Top 10 single “Burning Down the House.” The following tour was filmed by Jonathan Demme for the concert film “Stop Making Sense” (1984). “Little Creatures” (1985) became the band’s best-selling album, “True Stories” (1986) served as the soundtrack to Byrne’s film of the same name, and “Naked” (1988) became the group’s final studio album. Byrne left the band in 1991 and Talking Heads disbanded. The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2002, reuniting briefly to perform. The 47th anniversary of “Fear of Music” places the album at the midpoint of Talking Heads’ three-album run with Eno, between “More Songs About Buildings and Food” and “Remain in Light.”
items._cn_summary: 本文为Talking Heads第三张录音室专辑的周年纪念资讯，详述了专辑的录制背景、曲目顺序、制作人员及乐队简史。1979年发行的《Fear of Music》由Brian Eno与乐队共同制作，融合了后朋克的冷峻质感、放克与迪斯科节奏，Robert Fripp在开场曲中贡献吉他。录音在长岛城的阁楼与多家纽约工作室完成，Greg Calbi负责母带处理。文章还回顾了乐队从罗德岛设计学院时期至1980年代商业巅峰的历程，以及Eno将Fela Kuti西非复合节奏引入《Remain in Light》的脉络。整体为编年史式新闻稿，未涉及深度音乐分析或美学探讨。

items.body: Alchera Vision has released the Castle Party 2026 compilation, a limited digiCD tied to the annual Castle Party festival at Bolków Castle, Poland. The release is out this week, on 7-8 August 2026. It comes in a 3-panel digipak with 19 tracks running 71 minutes, and is distributed in Europe through Audioglobe. Castle Party 2026 by Various Artists The “Castle Party 2026” compilation continues an annual series that Alchera Vision has produced alongside the festival since at least 2014, pairing festival headliners with newer acts and offering radio edits, remixes, video versions and tracks making their first appearance on CD. The 2026 edition mixes acts who played this year’s Bolków edition with others connected to the festival’s wider circle, spanning EBM, darkwave, gothic rock, post-punk and industrial styles. Castle Party 2026 compilation tracklist Empathy Test – “Monsters” (Radio Edit) – 04:00 Ash Code – “Nostalgia” – 03:13 A Projection – “No Control” – 03:02 Mayflower Madame – “A Foretold Ecstasy” – 04:36 Long Night – “Ghost” – 03:55 The Last Digital Angel – “One” – 02:38 Tribulation – “Drink The Love Of God” – 02:56 Merciful Nuns – “Elysene” – 03:19 Moonspell – “Opium” (Radio Edit) – 02:46 Agonised Too – “Lurking Fear” (Video Version) – 04:11 This Morn’ Omina – “(The) Rûach (of God)” [CCF] – 04:57 Rue Oberkampf – “Eternity” – 04:21 Denuit – “Wounded Heart” (Mila Dietrich Remix) – 03:00 Sierra Veins – “My Poison” – 03:27 Unter Null – “Coming Up To Breathe” – 05:32 Dawn Of Ashes – “Viral Decay” – 04:14 Hocico – “Hey Tú!” (with Prayers) – 04:12 Xotox – “Leben und Sterben für Musik aus Strom” (EXT!ZE Remix) – 03:33 She Pleasures Herself – “Last Goodbye” – 03:42 Several acts on the “Castle Party 2026” compilation played this year’s festival at Bolków, among them Empathy Test, Hocico, Denuit, A Projection, She Pleasures Herself, Long Night, This Morn’ Omina, Agonised Too and Rue Oberkampf. Sierra Veins, who also performed at the 2026 edition, contributes “My Poison” to the tracklist. About Castle Party Castle Party began on 20 August 1994 at Grodziec Castle, drawing around 300 people to see five Polish bands early in their careers: Moonlight, Daimonion, T.R.H., Pornografia and Fading Colours. The festival outgrew Grodziec within a few years and moved to Bolków Castle in 1997, the enclosed medieval courtyard setting it has kept since. Attendance grew from roughly 800 in 1995 to around 4,000 by 1999, when Clan of Xymox headlined. Castle Party became a three-day event in 2000, and its 2026 edition ran across four days, from 16 to 19 July, with a line-up including Moonspell, Diary of Dreams, Hocico, Empathy Test, Rotersand, Covenant and XOTOX across the Castle Stage and Park Stage. Side-Line covered the full 2026 timetable in May and published a four-day report from Bolków after the festival. Held annually at Bolków Castle in Poland, it is described as the biggest festival of its genre in Eastern Europe. About Alchera Vision Alchera Vision is the Polish label behind the annual Castle Party compilation series, releasing new editions to coincide with the festival and distributing them in Europe through Audioglobe. Its back catalogue includes prior “Castle Party” compilations dating back to at least 2014, alongside catalogue numbers such as the TRAITRS debut album “Rites and Ritual”, first released via the label in May 2017. The “Castle Party 2026” compilation extends that yearly series, again drawing its tracklist from artists connected to the festival’s line-up and circle.
